projectDescription: A progressive knowledge tree for understanding reality through connected domains.

nodes.label: Knowledge
nodes.description: A living map of how we understand the world through evidence, reasoning, and shared meaning.

nodes.label: Science
nodes.description: Explains the natural world through observation, models, and testable hypotheses.

nodes.label: Mathematics
nodes.description: The language of structure, quantity, and logical relationships.

nodes.label: Language
nodes.description: How humans represent ideas, communicate meaning, and shape understanding.

nodes.label: Technology
nodes.description: Applied knowledge: turning ideas into tools, systems, and capabilities.

nodes.label: Philosophy
nodes.description: Examines truth, reasoning, ethics, and how we justify what we believe.

nodes.label: Scientific Method
nodes.description: A cycle of forming hypotheses, testing them, and refining explanations.

nodes.label: Matter and Energy
nodes.description: Core physical concepts describing what things are and how they change.

nodes.label: Life Systems
nodes.description: How living organisms are organized, adapt, and interact with environments.

nodes.label: Hypothesis and Falsifiability
nodes.description: What makes a scientific claim testable and open to being proven wrong.

nodes.label: Experiment Design
nodes.description: How controls, variables, and measurement improve reliability of conclusions.

nodes.label: Atomic Structure
nodes.description: How atomic composition helps explain material properties and reactions.

nodes.label: Energy Transfer
nodes.description: How energy moves through systems via heat, work, and transformation.

nodes.label: Ecosystem Dynamics
nodes.description: How interactions between organisms and environment shape stability and change.

nodes.label: Evolution by Selection
nodes.description: How variation and selection produce adaptation over generations.

nodes.label: Logical Reasoning
nodes.description: Drawing sound conclusions from clear premises and valid argument forms.

nodes.label: Patterns and Functions
nodes.description: Describing change and relationships between quantities.

nodes.label: Probability and Uncertainty
nodes.description: Reasoning under uncertainty using chance, likelihood, and expectation.

nodes.label: Deduction vs Induction
nodes.description: Understanding when certainty is possible and when inference is probabilistic.

nodes.label: Proof as Explanation
nodes.description: Seeing proof not only as verification, but as insight into why statements hold.

nodes.label: Function Modeling
nodes.description: Using functions to model growth, decay, and recurring real-world behavior.

nodes.label: Rate of Change
nodes.description: Interpreting how quickly quantities change and what that implies.

nodes.label: Conditional Probability
nodes.description: Updating likelihoods when new information becomes available.

nodes.label: Risk and Decision Making
nodes.description: Balancing outcomes and uncertainty to make better decisions.

nodes.label: Meaning and Interpretation
nodes.description: How words map to concepts and why context changes meaning.

nodes.label: Argument and Rhetoric
nodes.description: How language persuades, clarifies, or distorts reasoning.

nodes.label: Communication Clarity
nodes.description: Structuring ideas so others can understand and respond effectively.

nodes.label: Ambiguity and Precision
nodes.description: Recognizing unclear language and reformulating with precision.

nodes.label: Framing Effects
nodes.description: How wording influences judgment without changing core facts.

nodes.label: Explanation Design
nodes.description: Adapting explanations to audience knowledge and goals.

nodes.label: Computation
nodes.description: How problems are represented and solved through algorithms.

nodes.label: Systems Design
nodes.description: Building reliable systems from interacting components and constraints.

nodes.label: AI Foundations
nodes.description: Core ideas behind machine learning, model behavior, and limitations.

nodes.label: Algorithmic Thinking
nodes.description: Decomposing problems into clear, executable steps.

nodes.label: Performance Trade-offs
nodes.description: Balancing speed, memory, and complexity in solution design.

nodes.label: Reliability and Failure Modes
nodes.description: Anticipating failures and designing systems that degrade gracefully.

nodes.label: Feedback Loops
nodes.description: Using measurement and iteration to improve system behavior over time.

nodes.label: Generalization
nodes.description: How models perform on unseen cases, not just training examples.

nodes.label: Bias and Limits
nodes.description: Understanding where AI systems can be misleading, unfair, or brittle.

nodes.label: Epistemology
nodes.description: What it means to know something and how knowledge is justified.

nodes.label: Ethics
nodes.description: How we reason about right action, responsibility, and values.

nodes.label: Philosophical Logic
nodes.description: Evaluating claims, arguments, and assumptions with rigor.

nodes.label: Belief and Justification
nodes.description: Distinguishing justified belief from opinion or intuition.

nodes.label: Truth Under Uncertainty
nodes.description: How to reason and act when certainty is impossible.

nodes.label: Consequences and Duties
nodes.description: Comparing outcome-based and principle-based ethical reasoning.

nodes.label: Reasoning Fallacies
nodes.description: Recognizing recurring errors that weaken arguments.
